paper.title_en: The ALMA carbon monoxide supernova (ACOS) survey II. Turbulent giant molecular clouds at the positions of core-collapse supernovae
paper.abstract_en: Context. Study of cold molecular hydrogen gas (hereafter molecular gas) provides crucial insights into its interplay with star-forming regions. However, the connection between molecular gas turbulence and the sites of massive star ($> 8~\rm{M}_{\odot}$) explosions as core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) remains unexplored. Aims. We measure for the first time the turbulence of molecular gas in environments of CCSNe, with the aim to constrain the nature of their progenitors. Methods. In order to reach spatial resolutions of giant molecular cloud (GMC) sizes ($\sim 100~\rm{pc}$), we collected ALMA carbon monoxide $J = 2 \rightarrow 1$ spectral line ($\sim 230.54~\rm{GHz}$) observations (as a tracer of molecular gas) at the locations of 33 nearby CCSNe ($< 100~\rm{Mpc}$). Results. We found that CCSNe prefer molecular gas regions with high velocity dispersion compared to the average of their host galaxies. Conclusions. For CCSN progenitors, this observational evidence supports their increased formation in regions of high densities and/or their binary nature.
